rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

All pairs are comfortably resolved, so halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty. Keeping the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed reveals how the critical pairs respond to gradient steepness.

The critical cluster loses substantial resolution when the gradient is shortened. An intermediate duration should recover much of that separation while retaining a smaller time penalty than the initial run.

Keep the intermediate gradient and test temperature-dependent selectivity in the remaining critical pair. Higher temperature should shorten retention, potentially allowing full resolution without a time penalty.

The central cluster appears to undergo an elution-order reversal as temperature increases. Testing 55 C may separate that pair again while keeping the neighboring pairs resolved and the last peak below the time-penalty threshold.

Use a slightly steeper gradient than injection 5 to move the temperature-reversed critical pair just above R = 1.5 while preserving its neighboring separation. The final organic fraction remains well above the observed elution window, so all ten compounds should elute without a time penalty.

Increase gradient steepness slightly again: the last change improved the critical pair, which now needs only a small gain to reach R = 1.5. The neighboring pair retains some resolution margin, and the shorter retention should avoid any time penalty.

Injection 7 has reached the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Test one further increase in steepness to see whether it preserves that score with shorter retention and slightly greater separation of the critical pair.

The maximum CRF is already secured. Test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to determine whether shifting the gradient window improves the resolution margin of the two closest pairs while retaining a penalty-free run.

Slightly reduce the slope from injection 9 to recover resolution in the newly limiting pair while preserving the improved separation of the other close pair. This may provide a larger minimum-resolution margin at the maximum CRF already achieved.

One further decrease in gradient slope should raise the limiting pair above R = 1.5 while leaving the other close pair resolved. The predicted last-peak time remains comfortably below the time-penalty threshold, potentially matching maximum CRF with more resolution margin.

Test a higher starting fraction with a compensating shallower slope to improve the central pair’s resolution without sacrificing its neighboring separation. Injection 11 remains a maximum-score benchmark; this run explores whether that score can be maintained with greater resolution margin.

Reduce the slope to recover separation of the limiting pair while retaining the improved resolution of the other central pair. The last peak is projected near 9.1 minutes, with the final organic fraction still above its elution window.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 13 to increase the limiting pair’s resolution toward that of the other close pair. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially preserving maximum CRF with a larger minimum-resolution margin.
Test a slope between injections 13 and 14 to balance the two closest pairs near R = 1.7. This should preserve the maximum CRF while slightly shortening retention relative to injection 14.

Test a slightly shallower slope than injection 11 with the same starting fraction and temperature. This should retain full resolution and maximum CRF while keeping the first peak farther from the unretained region than in injection 15.

With maximum CRF already secured, explore 60 C for greater separation of the temperature-sensitive central pair. A shallower gradient and low starting organic fraction should help protect the neighboring pair, while higher temperature may keep the last peak near the penalty-free time window.

The 60 C shallow-gradient result offers little room to improve resolution without a time penalty. With maximum CRF already secured, test a much steeper gradient for a possible reversal and renewed separation of the limiting pair at substantially shorter retention.

Maximum CRF is already secured at 55 C; test a cooler selectivity regime for an alternative fully resolved method. This moderate gradient should keep all compounds observable and reveal whether cooling separates the central cluster without creating another critical pair.

Return to the established maximum-score region with a slope between injections 10 and 11. This should balance the two closest pairs above R = 1.5 while shortening retention slightly relative to injection 11.

Preserve injection 11’s starting composition, temperature, and gradient slope while trimming the endpoint to just beyond the last peak’s estimated elution composition. All peaks should remain within the gradient, maintaining maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Trim the solvent endpoint while using a slope close to injection 15, which gave the largest minimum-resolution margin among maximum-score runs. The last peak should elute near 9.3 minutes, before the gradient ends at the outlet, preserving full resolution without a time penalty.

Preserve the slope, starting fraction, and temperature of injection 8, the fastest maximum-score run, while trimming the gradient endpoint. The last peak’s estimated elution fraction is about 0.57, so all ten peaks should elute before the gradient ends and retain the maximum CRF.

Refine near the maximum-score methods with the largest resolution margins by slightly reducing the slope from injection 14. Both critical pairs should remain comfortably above R = 1.5, with the last peak predicted below the 10-minute time-penalty threshold.

Finish with a slightly steeper gradient than injection 13, targeting a shorter run while keeping both critical pairs above R = 1.5. The campaign has already reached the maximum CRF of 1.000; this final refinement should remain within that fully resolved, penalty-free region.
